title: Can Make Palindrome From Substring Queries
description: You are given a lowercase string `s` and an array `queries` where `queries[i] = [left, right, k]`. For each query, consider the substring `s[left..right]` (inclusive): you may rearrange its characters in any order and then replace up to `k` characters with any lowercase letter. Return a boolean array where the `i`-th entry is `true` if the substring can be turned into a palindrome, and `false` otherwise.
hints: After rearranging, only the parity (odd vs even count) of each of the 26 letters matters.
Maintain a prefix 26-bit XOR mask; the number of odd-frequency letters in [left, right] is popcount(prefix[right + 1] ^ prefix[left]), and you need oddCount // 2 replacements.

examples.explanation: Query [3,3,0] is "d" (already a palindrome); [1,2,0] is "bc" (needs 1 change); [0,3,1] is "abcd" (4 odd letters require 2 changes); [0,3,2] allows 2 changes; [0,4,1] is "abcda" (3 odd letters require 1 change).
With 0 replacements, "ly" cannot form a palindrome, while "b" with 1 replacement can.
All letters are identical so every substring is already a palindrome.
